title: Kobani Prison Fire Kills at Least 9 Amid Unrest Over Kurdish Fighter's Killing
detail: A riot and fire at a Kurdish-administered prison in Kobani (Ayn al-Arab) killed at least seven inmates by state media's count and nine according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (a toll SOHR later said reached 9-10 as two of the injured died of their wounds by September 17), with dozens more injured from burns and smoke inhalation. The unrest began after inmates rioted overnight, reportedly fearing a planned transfer of prisoners to a facility in Aleppo; the fire's exact cause remains officially unconfirmed. The riot followed a day of protests in Kobani over the killing of Sami Shekhmous Hiso, a former Kurdish fighter who was abducted and whose body was returned with gunshot wounds on Thursday, September 10. The Democratic Union Party (PYD) placed 'full responsibility' on the government and demanded an urgent, transparent investigation into both Hiso's death and the prison fire; Syria's Internal Security Forces said it had opened a formal inquiry. Presidential adviser and former SDF commander Mazloum Abdi visited Kobani on September 13 to meet local officials. The prison remains under Kurdish administration and has not yet been handed over to Damascus, underscoring frictions in the SDF integration process months after its formal dissolution.

media.caption: Syrian government forces and the country's Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces reached an integration agreement earlier in 2026, but Kobani prison remains under Kurdish administration
